label: Bi-directional XDCR between mobile clusters (Sync Gateway 4.0+)
type: Sync Gateway 4.0's native active-active XDCR support for mobile clusters: an architectural change from revision trees to version vectors (sgw:version-vector) that lets two Sync-Gateway-fronted Couchbase Server clusters replicate bidirectionally via ordinary Couchbase Server XDCR, rather than through Sync Gateway's own ISGR mechanism. Positioned in the docs as a simpler, more efficient alternative to sgw:inter-sync-gateway-replication for active-active mobile topologies (see relations/supersedes.json) - not a rename or extension of ISGR, and not the same feature as xdcr:active-active-with-app-services (Capella App Services' own bi-directional XDCR feature, gated at Server 7.6.6+/App Services 4.0+ with no Sync Gateway dependency at all; this concept is gated at Server 7.6.5+ and is Sync-Gateway-native). Do not confuse the two: both are called 'bi-directional XDCR' in their respective docs trees, but no page states they are the same mechanism, and their version gates differ (7.6.5+ here, 7.6.6+ there).
aliases_note: One round-28 record (sync/sync-with-couchbase-server.json) originally misfiled its 'Bi-directional XDCR is only supported in Sync Gateway 4.0' relation against xdcr:active-active-with-app-services; corrected during this round's reconciliation to point here instead - see that record's own reconciliation_note.
evidence: Sync Gateway 4.0 introduces support for bi-directional XDCR between active mobile clusters through an architectural change from revision trees to version vectors.
Sync Gateway 4.0 and later requires CBS 7.6.1+. Active-Active XDCR requires CBS 7.6.5+. Sync Gateway 3.x does not support Active-Active XDCR.

This relies on a change in how Sync Gateway tracks document revisions, transitioning from revision trees to version vectors, which enables consistent revision tracking across all participating clusters.
note: Recurrence 4 across product-notes/compatibility.json, server-compatibility/xdcr-active-active-eventing.json, server-compatibility/server-compatibility-xdcr.json and server-compatibility/server-compatibility-xdcr-mobile.json, all consistently spelled - genuine convergence, not a self-fork. Central to this round's ISGR-vs-XDCR coordinator decision (see reconciliation.md round 28): server-compatibility-xdcr.json's own record states this feature provides 'a simpler and more efficient alternative to Inter-Sync Gateway Replication', which server-compatibility-xdcr.json filed as a takesPrecedenceOver relation - a predicate-range mismatch (takesPrecedenceOver's own type is scoped to settings/config values overriding each other, not whole feature/mechanism supersession) corrected during reconciliation to a newly-minted supersedes relation instead. Requires enableCrossClusterVersioning on both clusters and reliesOnMechanism sgw:version-vector; does not affect sgw:channel-access-revocation or user/role configuration, which must still be configured separately on each cluster.
